info.title: Smart Task Management API
info.description: Projects, tasks, users and dashboard. Every response uses the BaseResponse envelope.

post.summary:
Rewrites a rough task description so it is grammatically correct, clearer, more professional and
actionable, and expands it when it is very short. Returns the original, the suggested text and up
to three notes about missing information. Nothing is saved: the client decides whether to apply it.
The text is sent to a third-party AI provider.

502.description: The AI provider returned output that failed validation.

503.description: The AI provider timed out, is busy or is unavailable.

post.summary: Creates a new account. New accounts are always team members.
Signs in. Returns an access token and sets the refresh-token cookie.
Exchanges the refresh-token cookie for a new access token, and rotates the cookie.
Signs out: revokes the refresh token and clears its cookie. Always succeeds.

get.summary:
Gets task counts by status and priority, overdue and pending counts, and the tasks due in the
next upcomingDays days (clamped to 1–30). Admins see everything, project
managers their own projects, team members their own tasks.
Lists the projects visible to the caller: all of them for admins, otherwise those they own or belong to.

post.summary: Creates a project owned by the caller.

get.summary: Gets a project with its owner, members and task counts.

put.summary: Replaces a project's name, description and dates.

delete.summary: Deletes a project and its tasks (soft delete).

post.summary: Adds an active user to the project. Adding an existing member does nothing.

delete.summary: Removes a member from the project. The owner cannot be removed.

get.summary: Lists one project's tasks, paged, filtered and sorted.

post.summary: Creates a task in the project. New tasks start as ToDo.

get.summary: Lists tasks across all projects visible to the caller, paged, filtered and sorted.
Gets a task with its project name and assignee.

put.summary: Replaces a task's title, description, priority and due date.

patch.summary: Moves a task to a new status, if the transition rules allow it. Admins, the project owner and the assignee may do this.
Assigns the task to a project member, or unassigns it when the assignee id is null.

put.summary: Updates the signed-in user's first and last name.

post.summary:
Changes the caller's password. The current password is required. Every other session is signed
out; this one gets a new access token and refresh cookie. Required first for a user whose password
an admin set (`mustChangePassword`); every other endpoint answers 403 `PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED` until then.

get.summary: Lists users, paged, filtered and sorted (admin only).

post.summary:
Creates an account with any role and an initial password. Self-registration only creates team
members; this is how an admin adds project managers or other admins directly.

get.summary: Finds active users by name or email, for member and assignee pickers (up to 20 results).
Gets a user by id (admin only).

patch.summary: Changes a user's role (admin only). Admins cannot demote themselves.

post.summary: Deactivates a user and revokes their refresh tokens (admin only). Admins cannot deactivate themselves.

Bearer.description: Paste the accessToken from POST /api/v1/auth/login (without the 'Bearer ' prefix).

tags.name: Ai
tags.description: AI assistance. Any signed-in user may call it; it never saves anything.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description:
Registration and session endpoints. They are anonymous because a caller has no valid access token
yet, or it has expired. The refresh token travels only in the `stms_refresh` HttpOnly cookie.

tags.name: Dashboard
tags.description: Dashboard statistics, scoped to the caller's role.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description:
Projects and their members. Any role may read (the service scopes what each user sees). Write
actions require the Admin or ProjectManager role; the service then checks that a project manager
owns the project.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description:
Tasks, both nested under their project (`projects/{projectId}/tasks`) and on their own
(`tasks/{id}`). Changing status is open to any signed-in user, because the assignee may do it.
The service decides who may change which task.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: The current user's profile, plus user administration for admins.
